content:
Apple TV swept 20 awards at the Creative Arts Emmys over two nights last week and added nine more tonight at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards. Here is the full list of winners.

  • Kate O'Flynn, Best Supporting Actress in a Comedy Series
  • Stephen Root, Best Supporting Actor in a Comedy Series
  • Matthew Rhys, Best Actor in a Comedy Series
  • Katie Dippold, Best Writing for a Comedy Series
  • Hiro Murai, Best Directing for a Comedy Series
  • Best Comedy Series
  • Rhea Seehorn, Best Actress in a Drama Series
  • Vince Gilligan, Best Writing for a Drama Series
  • Saul Metzstein, Best Directing for a Drama Series

Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson also plugged their upcoming Apple TV comedy, Brothers, while presenting the award for Best Comedy Series. The show is based on the long-running rumor that the two actors might be half-brothers.

Apple CEO John Ternus was also in attendance and showed off the all-new iPhone Duo in an interview with Deadline.

Including tonight's wins, Apple finished the 78th Emmys with 29 awards — the most ever for the company — including Best Commercial for the "I'm Not Remarkable" ad.

Widow's Bay alone took home 14 Emmys, surpassing last year's The Studio, which took 13. Both shows set the record in their first seasons on air.

In addition to the Apple TV winners, other awards handed out tonight included:

  • Best Actress in a Comedy Series: Jean Smart, Hacks
  • Best Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie: Matthew Rhys, The Beast in Me
  • Best Supporting Actress in a Drama Series: Allison Janney, The Diplomat
  • Best Competition Program: The Traitors
  • Best Actor in a Drama Series: Noah Wyle, The Pitt
  • Best Supporting Actor in a Drama Series: Tom Pelphrey, Task
  • Best Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie: Sally Field, Remarkably Bright Creatures
  • Best Variety Series: The Late Show with Stephen Colbert
  • Best Limited or Anthology Series: DTF St. Louis
  • Best Drama Series: The Pitt

Apple TV is available for $14.99 per month, or as part of the Apple One bundle. The platform offers a range of popular shows and movies, including Ted Lasso, Severance, The Studio, The Morning Show, Shrinking and Silo.
